reason: Re-opened via packet.js veda 45 --verse 4.40.5. Sāyaṇa opens on the verse as sauryā ṛc teaching that the god of the solar orb, the supreme Self present as the mind of all creatures (sarvaprāṇicittarūpasthitaḥ paramātmā) and the adjunct-free supreme Brahman are all one; then haṃsa/śuciṣat = Āditya in heaven, vasu/antarikṣasat = the same as wind (sa eva madhyasthāno vāyuḥ), hotā/vediṣat and atithi/duroṇasat = the same as Vedic and household fire, nṛṣat = paramātman as consciousness in men, ṛtam = Brahman. The paraphrase is carried. Plain sense: day.js shows 4.40 is the Dadhikravan hymn and 4.40.5 its last verse. verse.js ok (4.40.5, at [335,5]); entry-check ok. Only quibble: the pronoun “them” grammatically points at the dwellings, while Sāyaṇa identifies the dwellers (the one being in each seat) as Sun, wind and fire; a reader takes the sense, so not refuted.
better: Tighter: “...Sāyaṇa, on 4.40.5, reads the one who dwells in each place as the Sun, then as wind and fire, and the Sun as one with the Self in every creature and with the unconditioned Brahman.” (check the cap)
